source.title: Task Discovery: Finding the Tasks that Neural Networks Generalize on
source.authors: Andrei Atanov; Andrei Filatov; Teresa Yeo; Ajay Sohmshetty; Amir Zamir

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures agreement in predictions between independently trained networks, not similarity between their internal representations or distances. It cites work on representational similarity and convergent learning but does not test or rely on representational convergence.
record.gate_note: The study's agreement score is a prediction-agreement measure on held-out images. It is related to, but distinct from, the representational alignment in the claim versions, so rows are recorded under fits_no_version. Results about discovered task similarity, test accuracy, and adversarial splits are not results about representational convergence.
record.test_reason: The study measures agreement between the predictions of networks retrained with different seeds (agreement score), not similarity of internal representations, features or subspaces. It cites convergent-learning and representational-similarity work (e.g. ref 53, CKA, SVCCA) only in related work. Prediction agreement across seeds is a related but different construct from V3's shared features, so its findings belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also stress that discovered tasks reflect inductive biases and can build adversarial train-test splits that sharply lower test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures agreement between network predictions across training runs; it does not apply a method for measuring representational-distance alignment.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction agreement varies with task type, number of training images, source of stochasticity, architecture, and test-data domain.

fits_no_version.finding: Prediction agreement between seed-varied networks is high for human-labelled tasks and near chance for random labels. It depends on architecture, training-set size and which source of stochasticity is varied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functional (prediction) agreement across training runs depends on the task labelling, the architecture and the data amount. It is distinct from representational convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Discovered-task agreement stays stable across out-of-distribution test domains, while human-task agreement is more volatile.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prediction agreement across runs depends on the test-data domain, and how strongly depends on the task.

fits_no_version.finding: Tasks induced by random-initialization networks reach agreement of about 0.85. Cross-architecture correlation of agreement scores falls from 0.8 to 0.17 when discovered tasks are included.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conclusions about which architectures share inductive biases depend on the task set evaluated.

record.problems: The measured outcome is prediction agreement rather than representational alignment. Many plotted values are not stated numerically in the text; the paper's main agreement-score experiments use CIFAR-10 and specified image datasets.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's test-domain plots report separate distributions for multiple datasets and task groups (Section 5.3, Figure 5); only the text-level aggregate findings relevant to prediction agreement are recorded, not each plotted dataset-specific value. Task-discovery optimization outcomes, task-label similarity, and adversarial-split accuracies are omitted because they do not measure representational convergence.

untested.parts: Scale or capability trends; cross-architecture representational alignment.
Shared features or subspaces across seeds. Only output agreement across seeds is measured.
Linear maps, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Metric, setting or input dependence of representational similarity. The test-domain dependence shown concerns prediction agreement only.
Incompleteness or plateau of representational alignment and its causes.

record.verdict_notes: This is a prediction-agreement study and has no bearing on representational convergence versions. Appendix A TinyImageNet results (discovered tasks AS>0.8, human binary tasks AS<0.65) and the adversarial-split accuracies (Table 1) are also outside the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Model scale and capability; alignment of internal representations across architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
Cross-modal image-caption representation alignment and its relationship to model performance.
Shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks; the study measures prediction agreement, not feature or subspace convergence.
Mapping or stitching representations, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Dependence of representational convergence on similarity metrics, settings, or inputs. The paper studies prediction agreement under task and test-data changes instead.
Whether representational alignment is incomplete or explained by shared training data or objectives.
